Build: `cmake --build build/arm64 --config RelWithDebInfo --target shell_integration_harness` (node on PATH: /Users/kenneth/.nvm/versions/node/v24.13.0/bin). Run: `build/arm64/tests/shell/RelWithDebInfo/JusPrinShellHarness.app/Contents/MacOS/JusPrinShellHarness --printer-setup`.

Backtrace under lldb (`lldb --batch -o "run --printer-setup" -k "bt 25" -- <harness>`):
frame #0 wxEvtHandler::SafelyProcessEvent(wxEvent&)
frame #1 wxWebView::SendScriptResult(void*, bool, wxString const&) const
frame #2 block in wxWebViewWebKit::RunScriptAsync(...)
then WebKit IPC completion handlers on the main run loop.

So a WKWebView's RunScriptAsync reply is delivered after its wxWebView/event handler was destroyed. Likely candidates: the temporary task chat panel (src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/PrinterSetup/PrinterPanel.cpp: close(), tear_down_runtime(), the m_retired / release timer path) tearing down a web view that still has an async script in flight, or the harness's PrinterWindow / Home web views. The repo already documents a related macOS trap: never delete a web view while wxGetApp().is_adding_script_handler() (see tear_down_runtime's comment). Reproduce first, find which web view dies with a script pending, and fix the ordering in the owner (defer destruction until pending script replies are delivered, or stop issuing RunScriptAsync on a view being torn down) rather than suppressing the crash. Verify `--printer-setup`, `--task-chat` and the default mode all pass afterwards, and follow AGENTS.md (error-handling discipline, fork stewardship for any file outside src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin).

```
cmake -B build/arm64 -G "Ninja Multi-Config" -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release \
  -DCMAKE_OSX_ARCHITECTURES=arm64 -DCMAKE_OSX_DEPLOYMENT_TARGET=15.0 \

  -DCMAKE_AR=/opt/homebrew/opt/llvm/bin/llvm-ar -DCMAKE_RANLIB=/opt/homebrew/opt/llvm/bin/llvm-ranlib
```

The two `CMAKE_AR`/`CMAKE_RANLIB` flags are required on a FRESH build dir:
without them Apple's ar is used and liblibslic3r_gui.a (>4 GiB in
RelWithDebInfo) fails to archive. They only work at first configure, not on
reconfigure. Full story: agent-docs/macos-build-troubleshooting.md. See
[[liblibslic3r-gui-4gib-ar-limit]].

does not build the web pages. Also build `--target jusprin_web jusprin_catalogs`
(needs node on PATH: /Users/kenneth/.nvm/versions/node/v24.13.0/bin). Without
them resources/jusprin/{home,agent}/index.html are missing, no web views are
created, and the harness silently tests something else (printer panel starts
shown; web-view crashes vanish).

`BUILD_TESTS=ON` is required or the tests/ tree (workspace, shell targets) is
not generated. Build with `cmake --build build/arm64 --config RelWithDebInfo
--target <targets>`. wxWidgets 3.3 sources for API verification live under
/Users/kenneth/Projects/OrcaSlicer/deps/build/arm64/dep_wxWidgets-prefix/.

CWD TRAP (cost real time once): the harness resets the Bash cwd to the main
repo /Users/kenneth/Projects/JusPrin between turns, so a *relative*
`cmake --build build/arm64` silently builds the MAIN repo's build dir, not the
worktree's — the worktree binary then runs stale code and a re-fix looks like it
"didn't take". Always pass the worktree build dir as an ABSOLUTE path to
`cmake --build /…/.claude/worktrees/<wt>/build/arm64 …`, and run test binaries by
absolute path. Also: `cmake --build --target <one_exe>` may relink against a
stale lib without recompiling a changed .cpp in that lib — build the app target
(e.g. OrcaSlicer) too so the lib recompiles; verify with
`grep -c '<file>.cpp.o' build.log`. Editing tools (Edit/Write) use absolute
paths so source edits land correctly regardless of cwd.

rebuild the web pages, so a harness run after an edit to AgentUI (for example
printerInstructions.ts) loads the old bundle. Six --printer-live runs were
wasted this way. After any page edit, build `jusprin_web` explicitly and check

name: webview-destroyed-mid-handler-install
description: "macOS crash when a wxWebView is destroyed while Orca's deferred AddScriptMessageHandler waits in a nested wxYield; guard with is_adding_script_handler()"
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: 81c54418-2f00-4c26-a129-4ddda1795da2
  modified: 2026-09-18T23:36:12.188Z
---

Found 2026-09-18 (printer-setup shell harness exit 139 after PASS, at 0e55c4f9be).

Orca's `WebView::CreateWebView` (src/slic3r/GUI/Widgets/WebView.cpp) installs each view's "wx" message handler from a `CallAfter`. On macOS wx's `AddScriptMessageHandler` then runs a *synchronous* `RunScript`, which spins `wxYield` until WebKit answers, with `GUI_App::is_adding_script_handler()` true. Any pending CallAfter can run inside that yield. If it destroys that web view, WebKit later cancels the reply and calls `SendScriptResult` on the freed view → segfault in `wxEvtHandler::SafelyProcessEvent`. The JusPrin bridge's own sends are NOT the cause: `WebView::RunScript` on Mac uses `WKWebView_evaluateJavaScript` with no completion.

**Why:** a panel opened and closed within one event-loop turn (harness, or fast clicks) tears down before the install finishes.

**How to apply:** never delete a web view (or its owner) while `is_adding_script_handler()` is true. Hide it, cut its callbacks, and retry on a timer, as `PrinterPanel::tear_down_runtime` does (branch claude/printer-panel-exit-crash) and as `GUI_App::run_wizard` already did. Any other short-lived AgentWebView owner needs the same guard. Related: [[workspace-harness-never-post-inits-on-mac]], [[agent-setup-embedded-in-printer-dialog]].

name: workspace-harness-never-post-inits-on-mac
description: "On macOS the workspace adapter harness never reaches GUI_App::post_init; closing its frame crashes, so it exits via ExitMainLoop unless post_initialized()"
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: ed4bbcf2-a467-44f4-bceb-b20f93cd25d8
  modified: 2026-09-17T16:28:53.409Z
---

Found 2026-09-17 while fixing the journey-tools branch (merged to jusprin-newui as 35eb1b4a59).

`tests/workspace/real_adapter_harness.cpp` does its work in one synchronous run. On macOS, Orca adds each web view's script handler from a CallAfter (`src/slic3r/GUI/Widgets/WebView.cpp`) that runs a script and waits on the page in a nested event loop. In this harness the first one never returns, so `is_adding_script_handler()` stays true, the later views pile up in the static `g_delay_webviews`, and `post_init` (gated on that flag in `GUI_App.cpp`) never runs, even if the harness waits for it (it times out at 180 s).

Closing the main frame ends that wait; the deferred view setup (use-after-free on destroyed views) and then `post_init` (on a destroyed frame) run and segfault (exit 139) after `HARNESS RESULT PASS`. The harness therefore closes the frame only when `post_initialized()` (true on Windows, where the handler is added synchronously) and otherwise calls `ExitMainLoop()`.

**Why:** a Windows fix switched the exit to `Close(true)` and made every macOS run crash; an Orca-side fix (drop destroyed views from `g_delay_webviews`) removed only one of the two crashes.

**How to apply:** if the workspace harness crashes on exit, look here first; don't make it wait for post_init. The shell harness is unaffected because its checks are asynchronous. Related: [[orca-inherited-teardown-crash]], [[background-bash-timeout-kills-builds]].

description: "A run_in_background Bash build dies at the tool timeout (ninja prints \"interrupted by user\", exit 130); launch long builds with nohup and watch the log instead"
metadata:

---

A `cmake --build` started with the Bash tool's `run_in_background` is still
bound by that call's `timeout` (default 120 s, max 600 s). When it fires the
build log ends with `ninja: build stopped: interrupted by user.` and `exit=130`,
which looks like a human Ctrl-C but is the harness. Seen 2026-09-14 on a
725-step JusPrin rebuild.

**Why:** the notification says "completed" and the log shows no compiler
error, so it is easy to misread as a finished build; the changed files had not
compiled at all.

**How to apply:** for anything longer than a few minutes, start it detached
(`nohup sh -c "cmake --build … > log 2>&1; echo exit=\$? >> log" & disown`),
then arm a Monitor on the log that reports progress and the `exit=` line. Check
`grep -c '<file>.cpp.o' log` before trusting the result. Related:
[[track-wall-clock-on-background-work]], [[jusprin-worktree-build]].

# CLAUDE.md

OrcaSlicer — open-source C++17 3D slicer. wxWidgets GUI, CMake build system.

## Error handling discipline

- Do not catch an error merely because it can be caught. Catch only when the code can recover, translate the error at an abstraction boundary, or add context that is essential for diagnosis. Logging alone is not recovery.
- Represent expected states with normal control flow, not exceptions.
- Never turn an invariant violation or an "impossible" state into success or a silent no-op. Fix the invalid transition at the layer that owns the decision and let unexpected failures propagate to Sentry.
- Avoid duplicating defensive checks across layers. Keep lower-level operations strict, with their preconditions enforced by the caller that owns the workflow.
- If concurrency makes an invalid state reachable, fix the ordering or synchronization instead of suppressing the resulting error.
- Suppress an error only when it is genuinely expected and safely recoverable; document the reason and cover it with a test. Never broadly swallow unexpected errors.
- Prefer removing the root cause over reducing the visibility of its symptoms. Tests should encode valid transitions and assert that invalid ones remain visible.

## Build Commands

```bash
# macOS
cmake --build build/arm64 --config RelWithDebInfo --target all --

# Linux
cmake --build build --config RelWithDebInfo --target all --

# Windows (replace %build_type% with Debug/Release/RelWithDebInfo)
cmake --build . --config %build_type% --target ALL_BUILD -- -m
```

Node/npm is required to build the Agent and Home pages, or configure with `-DJUSPRIN_BUILD_WEB=OFF` and supply the bundles.

## Testing

Catch2 framework. Tests in `tests/` directory.

```bash
cd build && ctest --output-on-failure           # all tests
ctest --test-dir ./tests/libslic3r              # individual suite
ctest --test-dir ./tests/fff_print
```

Printer UI without hardware: `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Testing/README.md` (Bambu in-process fake). Isolated `--datadir`; do not drive another JusPrin instance.

## Code Style

- C++17, selective C++20. PascalCase classes, snake_case functions/variables
- `#pragma once` for headers. Smart pointers and RAII preferred
- Parallelization via TBB — be mindful of shared state

## Key Entry Points

- App startup: `src/OrcaSlicer.cpp`
- Slicing pipeline: `src/libslic3r/Print.cpp`
- All print/printer/material settings: `src/libslic3r/PrintConfig.cpp`
- GUI: `src/slic3r/GUI/`
- Core algorithms: `src/libslic3r/` (GCode/, Fill/, Support/, Geometry/, Format/, Arachne/)
- Printer profiles: `resources/profiles/[manufacturer].json`

## JusPrin Production UI

- Start with `agent-docs/jusprin/README.md` for the canonical product definition, production architecture, verification method, Orca integration guidance, and design system.
- Before editing any file outside `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/`, read `agent-docs/jusprin/fork-stewardship.md`. Every line changed in an OrcaSlicer-owned file is a line this fork re-resolves at every rebase, so those changes must be small, product-neutral, additive where possible, and accompanied by the rebase evidence that document requires.
- Experimental plans, probes, screenshots, logs, and temporary UI code remain on `jusprin-v2-poc`. Use `agent-docs/jusprin/poc-reference.md` for exact commit and path pointers; do not cherry-pick the POC wholesale.
- Curated brand and semantic UI assets live under `resources/jusprin/`.
- Before writing or changing any UI code, native or Agent page, follow "Writing UI code" in `agent-docs/jusprin/design-system.md`: every color, radius, font, and control size comes from the token file through `ShellTheme`, the shell recipes, or the CSS variables. A value with no token gets a token and a guard first, never a literal.
- Temporary working docs (handoffs, findings, plans written for another agent) stay untracked: never commit them, and never add them to `.gitignore` or `.git/info/exclude`. Untracked files in `git status` are how Kenneth tracks work that isn't finished.

## Critical Constraints

- **Backward compatibility required** for .3mf project files and printer profiles
- **Cross-platform** — all changes must work on Windows, macOS, and Linux
- Profile/format changes need version migration handling
- Dependencies built separately in `deps/build/`, then linked to main app

## Code review focus areas

- Changes must not cause regressions in existing functionality, defaults, profiles, or project compatibility.
- Features gated by options must not affect existing behavior when those options are disabled.
- Changes should follow the existing code style and architecture. Architectural changes should be justified in code comments and the PR description.
- Add helper functions or utilities only when existing code cannot reasonably be reused. Avoid duplication.
- Changes to OrcaSlicer-owned files must be additive where possible. Rewriting an upstream function, or reimplementing upstream behavior beside it, needs explicit justification in the PR description.
- When an upstream line is deleted or relocated, say where it went and what a future rebase must carry into the new home.
- Keep code concise and clear. Manually simplify AI generated bloated codes before review.
- Include targeted tests or documented verification for behavior changes, especially in slicing logic, profiles, formats, and GUI defaults.

content.text:
The `--printer-setup` crash is fixed, and it wasn't the temporary task chat panel. The web view that died was the browser inside Home's printer window (`Home::PrinterWindow`, the separate window that shows a print host's own web page). After the fix, `--printer-setup` passed on 5 of 6 runs; the sixth ended early without a crash or a failed check (details below). `--task-chat` and the default mode both pass.

**Root cause** (confirmed with lldb breakpoints on the web view's destructor and `RunScriptAsync`)
1. The harness opens a printer window. On macOS, the new web view queues its script-handler install as a `CallAfter`.
2. Home's backend goes out of scope and calls `window->Destroy()`. For a top-level window, wx doesn't delete it then; it queues the deletion for the next idle.
3. The queued install runs first. It waits for WebKit inside a nested `wxYield`, the idle processing runs inside that wait, and the window and its web view are deleted mid-install.
4. WebKit's reply arrives during the 3 s wait after `host_attempt_starts_waiting`. It is delivered to the freed view, which crashes in `SendScriptResult`.

The existing `is_adding_script_handler()` guard (the one `PrinterPanel::tear_down_runtime` uses) wouldn't have caught this, because the install hadn't started yet when `Destroy()` was called.

**Fix** (all in `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Home/`, so no Orca-owned files change)
- `PrinterWindow::close()` deletes the page view right away, but only when no web view is mid-install. Deleting it right away also discards an install it has queued but not started, because wx drops a handler's pending events in `~wxEvtHandler`. The frame, now empty, is then destroyed the normal way.
- If some view is mid-install, the window hides and retries every 50 ms.
- Home's backend and the title-bar close button both go through `close()`.
- A new `closing()` flag stops a second click from raising a window that is on its way out; the click opens a new window instead.

**Test added** in `tests/shell/shell_harness.cpp`: open a printer window, close it before its install runs, click again, then wait 3 s. In practice this exercised the wait-and-retry path, because another view happened to be mid-install at that moment. With the old `Destroy()` put back temporarily, the run crashes with exit 139 inside this new section, so the check catches the bug on its own.

**Results**

| Run | Result |
|---|---|
| `--printer-setup` at 9477a95eeb, no fix | exit 139, reproduced under lldb |
| `--printer-setup` with fix | 5 of 6 runs `PASS failures=0`, 192 checks, about 231 s each |
| `--task-chat` | `PASS failures=0` |
| default mode | `PASS failures=0` |

**Things to know**
- **One unexplained early exit.** One of the six `--printer-setup` runs stopped cleanly after `timeout_fixture_starts_attempt`: the main loop returned 0, with no failed check and no crash. That is in the Bambu connection checks, well after the printer-window code. It didn't happen again in the next four runs, so I don't know the cause.
- **Remaining gap in Orca code.** For PrusaLink and PrusaConnect hosts, `PrinterWebView::SendAPIKey` re-adds the script handler synchronously without setting `is_adding_script_handler()`. A close that lands during that short wait could still hit the same crash. The harness uses a Moonraker host, so it doesn't exercise that path.
- **Where the work is.** The changes are uncommitted on branch `claude/printer-setup-harness-crash`, cut from jusprin-newui 9477a95eeb, in my worktree `.claude/worktrees/modest-wozniak-151655`. It has its own fresh build. The only other file touched is the harness.
- **Build tooling.** Configuring a fresh build dir with Homebrew's cmake 4.1 fails on an Eigen version check, so I used `/Applications/CMake.app` instead. I've saved that to memory.

The fix is committed and landed on jusprin-newui as `55b4066bc5` ("Close Home's printer window without crashing on macOS"). I haven't pushed it: jusprin-newui is now one commit ahead of `origin/jusprin-newui`. jusprin-newui hadn't moved since my branch was cut from it, so the landed code is identical to what I tested.

**What happened, in plain English**

Home can open a separate window that shows a printer's own web page. The test opened that window and closed it again almost immediately.

When a web page view is created on a Mac, the app queues a small setup step. That step asks the page's browser engine (WebKit) a question and then waits for the answer.

Closing the window didn't delete it right away. It only scheduled the deletion for the next quiet moment. Then the setup step started, and while it waited for WebKit's answer, the app hit that quiet moment and deleted the window. When WebKit's answer arrived a few seconds later, it went to a view that no longer existed, and the app crashed.

The fix changes how the window closes. It now removes its web view straight away, but only when no web view is in the middle of that setup step; otherwise it hides and tries again 50 ms later. Removing the view also cancels its setup step if that hasn't started yet. A new test closes the window this quickly on purpose, and it crashes if the old behavior comes back.
